item.title: Swedish word of the day: orka
item.description: Orka is a word that you’ll hear a lot, and is a key to understanding young Swedish people’s conversations.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Thursday
item.description: Board member resigns from Migration Agency committee, funeral for 25-year-old murdered on Christmas Eve, and more news from Sweden on Thursday.

item.title: What are the proposed solutions to Sweden's teen deportation problem?
item.description: Teen deportations – the deportation of young adults after they turn 18 – is now Sweden's biggest political news story, with the opposition piling pressure on the government to take action, and the government parties split on how to respond.

item.title: Five great restaurants in Malmö for a fancy dinner date
item.description: Malmö has an impressive restaurant scene for its size, with options for all tastes and budgets. Here are some of the best fine dining spots in town.

item.title: Swedish citizenship almost impossible for stay-at-home partners under new law
item.description: The sweeping new changes to Swedish citizenship laws set to take effect on June 6th of this year include dramatically raised bars for the partners of Swedish citizens and a 20,000 kronor self-sufficiency requirement for all applicants.

item.title: How can you watch the 2026 Winter Olympics on Swedish TV
item.description: The Winter Olympics, which this year takes place in Milan and Cortina, is arguably a bigger deal for Swedes than the summer variety. Where can you follow the action on Swedish TV?

item.title: UPDATED: Your questions about Sweden's new citizenship law
item.description: Sweden's government announced more details of its new citizenship law on February 9th, which left our readers with a lot of questions. We've tried to find some answers.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: konstig
item.description: Do you think Swedish is a weird language? This word may come in handy.

item.title: Is it constitutional in Sweden to make laws apply retroactively?
item.description: Sweden's citizenship requirements, set to come into force on June 6th, 2026, will apply to all applications from that date ‒ even those which have already been submitted. Does this count as retroactive and, if so, is it constitutional?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Friday
item.description: Liberals call in opposition to urgent meeting on screen time, price of semla buns rises for another year, and other news from Sweden on Friday.
